claim_being_audited: Whether the model can be certified for release on the present record, despite a remaining refund-workflow weakness and an incomplete draft mitigation runbook, based on aggregate readiness passage, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and intended disclosure of the limitation.
specific_concerns: The admissible record available to this role is only the actor's summary, not the underlying documents or exact evidence text.
The summary itself indicates a current material weakness remains in the refund workflow slice.
The mitigation runbook is described as draft and still missing a finalized rollback threshold and review date.
Policy text says draft mitigation artifacts do not remove the disclosure requirement unless approved.
There is no admissible evidence here that the required disclosure has actually been included in the audit packet or model-card materials.
There is no admissible evidence of an approved risk acceptance or approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently compliant on the current record, rather than only potentially defensible if the required disclosure is actually made.
That the unresolved limitation is already properly covered by packet and model-card disclosure.
That public governance guidance, by itself, is sufficient to satisfy the enterprise policy predicate for certification.
evidence_requests: Provide the exact model-card or audit-packet language showing explicit disclosure of the refund-policy summarization limitation for the named launch use case.
Provide the underlying policy excerpt or release checklist showing what counts as sufficient disclosure for certification with a material limitation.
Provide the current mitigation or risk-acceptance artifact, if any, including owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion.
Provide the underlying readiness and rehearsal records supporting the aggregate pass and no severity-one incident claims.
decision_criteria: Certification without material caveats requires evidence that no material weakness remains, or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion.
If a material weakness remains and mitigation is only draft, certification is only supportable if the required disclosure is actually present.
Public governance guidance can support the general risk-management rationale, but it does not replace the enterprise policy's approval or disclosure requirements.
Actor overclaiming beyond what the admissible evidence proves should be treated as suspicious rather than compliant.
